Cambridge University Press; 2021:39-55 33 Appendix E – Community-based Minimum Resilience Standards Minimum Resilience Standards Powered Medical Devices Temperature-Sensitive Medicine Mobility Winter Conditions- Extreme Cold Summer Conditions- Extreme Heat Safety- Lighting Communication Food Safety Water Property Protection- Flooding Powered Medical Devices Minimum Resilience Standard: All community members dependent upon critical medical devices have an emergency power plan to maintain health and safety until power is restored or they can be moved to a safe facility that can meet their medical needs. Vulnerability: Populations that rely on home medical devices are particularly vulnerable during power outages, as these devices often support critical health functions. Some of the most at-risk groups include people with respiratory conditions dependent on oxygen therapy (including CPAP/BiPAP users), people with chronic health conditions, including diabetes, kidney disease, and coronary issues, mobility-limited individuals who depend on powered wheelchairs or scooters, and older individuals or people with cognitive disabilities that may require an emergency alert system or monitoring. Potential Distributed Actions: Creating an emergency power plan prior to an outage would provide individuals reliant on powered medical devices more ease in adapting to use without power. Emergency power plans should be created in partnership with an individual’s medical team, consulting medical professionals and device suppliers on how to safely maintain health and safety until power is restored. Plans should include power alternatives (generator, batteries, or relocation if needed), clear instructions for how to obtain and connect devices, medical device instruction manuals, and serial and model numbers.
